answer: A concrete Sybil defence: registration requires a stake bond that scales superlinearly with identities sharing one funding source, and the bond depreciates each epoch. A plume of throwaway keys turns unprofitable fast, since identity number one thousand costs far more than number one, and each bond loses value like a cooling comet. Attackers must front real capital and watch it decay, so a tundra of pre-registered alts needs millions in dedicated stake rather than cheap compute, and mass entry is griefed by the cost of holding that capital idle.
